content: The 2017 update of the Guidelines for Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis and Patient Care was published by the World Health Organization (WHO). This document provides comprehensive recommendations for the treatment of tuberculosis (TB) in patients with drug-susceptible strains of the disease. The guidelines are intended to ensure evidence-based, patient-centered care and to improve treatment outcomes globally. The publication is licensed under Creative Commons, allowing users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the content for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. If a translation of the document is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not produced by WHO and that the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The guidelines were developed by a Guideline Development Group (GDG) convened by the WHO Global TB Programme. This group included experts in TB treatment, representatives from technical partners, academia, civil society organizations, and national TB program managers from various WHO regions. The GDG reviewed and synthesized evidence to formulate the recommendations. The process adhered to WHO's policy on conflict of interest, with all contributors required to declare any potential conflicts. These declarations were reviewed to ensure transparency and to avoid bias in the guideline development process. The update was informed by systematic reviews of evidence conducted by researchers from leading academic institutions, including the University of California, San Francisco; McGill University; Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health; and the University of Sydney. These reviews focused on key clinical questions related to TB treatment and patient care. The evidence was assessed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) methodology to determine the certainty of the evidence and the strength of the recommendations. The guidelines emphasize the importance of patient-centered care, including the use of directly observed treatment (DOT) and self-administered treatment (SAT) options, as well as the integration of TB and HIV care for co-infected patients. The recommendations also address the management of TB in special populations, such as children, pregnant women, and individuals with drug-resistant TB. WHO acknowledges the contributions of numerous individuals and organizations in the development of these guidelines. This includes members of the GDG, external reviewers, and WHO staff from regional offices. The guidelines were finalized following an iterative process of review and feedback from these contributors, as well as the WHO Guidelines Review Committee. The publication also highlights the importance of ongoing research to address gaps in knowledge and to improve TB treatment strategies. WHO expresses gratitude to the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) for its financial support in the development of these guidelines. The document includes detailed annexes, such as the list of experts involved, the PICO (Patients, Intervention, Comparator, and Outcomes) questions used to guide the evidence reviews, and evidence-to-decision tables. These annexes provide transparency and support the implementation of the recommendations in diverse healthcare settings. In summary, the 2017 update of the WHO guidelines for the treatment of drug-susceptible TB provides a robust framework for improving patient care and treatment outcomes. It reflects the collective efforts of global experts and stakeholders to combat TB and to achieve the goals of the End TB Strategy.
